summary: A 16-day relaxation-first road trip from Frankfurt am Main to Poreč, Croatia (Istria). Free accommodation in your own house, fuel covered by company. Week 1: gentle exploration of Istria's medieval hill towns, coastal gems, and natural beauty within 100 km of Poreč — all dog-friendly. Week 2: pure beach relaxation with your two old dogs. Budget of €1,000 for two people covering food and entry fees for 14 days on the ground (≈€71/day).
special_2026: September in Istria is post-peak season — beaches are half-empty, temperatures are perfect (22-27°C), and the sea is still warm at 22-24°C. The Vrsar Music Festival runs 10-13 September nearby. The famous Špancirfest in Varaždin runs late August to early September (check exact dates). Truffle season begins in September — peak Istrian truffle time!

flights.tip: Route: Frankfurt → München (scenic stop) → Salzburg → Bled (Slovenia) → Poreč. About 750 km total, easy 2-day drive with beautiful stops.

accommodations.name: Your own house in Poreč
accommodations.description: You own the house in Poreč — the whole trip is based from here. Familiar environment is ideal for two old dogs who need routine and comfort. Same base for both weeks, just different daily activities.

Breakfast stop near München (packed or highway rest stop)

Free truffle and wine tastings at local shops (several offer free samples)

Return to Poreč, rest with dogs
Self-catered dinner at home

daily_itinerary.title: Day Trip: Rovinj — Istria's Most Beautiful Coastal Town

activities.activity: Drive to Rovinj (35 km, 40 min) — park at city parking lot
Walk Rovinj's old town and harbor. Dogs welcome on leash. Free.
St. Euphemia Church — free entry, climb bell tower (€3) for best panorama
Lunch: take-away cevapi or burek from a local bakery (€5-7 each)
Walk the Zlatni Rt (Golden Cape) forest park — dog-friendly nature paths
Drive back to Poreč, rest
Self-catered dinner

daily_itinerary.title: Pula Roman Arena + Brioni National Park Views

activities.activity: Drive to Pula (55 km, 45 min)
Pula Arena (Roman amphitheater) — €10 entry, one of the best-preserved in world
Walk Pula's Forum, Temple of Augustus, Sergii Arch — all free, dogs welcome
Lunch: budget konoba (taverna) in Pula old town — local pasta or grilled fish ~€10-12
Scenic drive along the coast toward Brioni Islands viewpoint (free)
Return to Poreč, self-catered dinner

daily_itinerary.title: Lim Bay + Vrsar — Fjord & Fishing Village

Viewpoint over Lim Bay (free). Look for shellfish farms below
Continue to Vrsar (10 km) — charming fishing village, walk old town, free

transport_details.route_description: Frankfurt am Main → München (scenic) → Salzburg area → Lake Bled (Slovenia) → Poreč. Return: same route reverse. Total ~1,500 km round trip.
transport_details.vignette_info: Fuel covered by company, tolls covered by company. For reference: Austria requires vignette (€9.90 for 10-day), Slovenia requires vignette (€15 for 7-day). Croatia has toll roads (€15-20 per direction).

scenic_stops.name: Lake Bled, Slovenia
scenic_stops.description: Iconic alpine lake with island church. Dog-friendly lakeside path. Perfect halfway stretch.

scenic_stops.name: Postojna / Predjama Castle
scenic_stops.description: Dramatic cave castle — worth a quick detour if timing allows.

beaches:
1. Blue Moon (beach Bijela Uvala) — DESIGNATED DOG BEACH, paved paths, beach bars, best for swimming with dogs
2. Plaža Borik — 15-min walk from town, sand/pebble, shallow entry, dog-tolerant
3. Plaža Materada — quiet pebble coves, pinetree shade, very calm, good for old dogs
4. Červar-Porat — long beach, pine forest right to shore, very quiet in September
5. Lanterna — wide beach, shallow, developed resort area with amenities
events_september: Vrsar Music Festival (10-13 September) — just 10 km from Poreč. If arriving on the 12th, you might catch the tail end. Also: Špancirfest Varaždin (late Aug/early Sep). Regular farmers markets in Poreč every morning with local produce.
budget_tips: Self-catering is your biggest money-saver. Shopping at Konzum/Plodine for the week costs ~€50-60 for two people.
Ask for free truffle/wine tastings at shops in Motovun, Livade, and Grožnjan — it's customary and free.
Buy a fresh truffle in Livade (€5-10) and make pasta at home — a €50 restaurant experience for €8.
Poreč waterfront has free public barbecue spots — bring charcoal and grill local sausages/vegetables.
Bakery breakfast (burek, bread, pastries) costs €2-3 per person vs €10+ at a cafe.
September is off-peak — many konobe have affordable lunch menus (€8-12) that are cheaper than dinner.
Natural beaches are free. No sunbed fees needed — bring towels and an umbrella.
Fill reusable water bottles at home — tap water in Poreč is excellent.
Local markets in Poreč (morning) have the cheapest seasonal fruit, vegetables, and cheese.
